content.text: {"expertise":[{"text":"Reactive extrusion of starch–protein blends enables control of mechanical properties and oxygen barrier performance through systematic variation of barrel temperature, screw speed, and protein content.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-02373","field":"abstract","quote":"central composite design was used to map the effect of barrel temperature, screw speed, and sunflower protein concentrate content on mechanical and barrier properties"},{"id":"SYN-PUB-02398","field":"abstract","quote":"Pea protein isolate was melt-blended with corn starch at protein contents of 10, 20, and 30 wt% in a co-rotating twin-screw extruder"}]},{"text":"Citric acid acts as a reactive compatibiliser to cross-link starch and protein phases, improving tensile strength and reducing water vapour transmission rate while maintaining processability.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-02398","field":"abstract","quote":"Cross-linking between starch hydroxyl groups and protein amino acid residues was promoted by adding citric acid as a reactive compatibiliser"}]},{"text":"Processing parameters directly control oxygen transmission rate and mechanical properties in starch–protein systems, with scale-up requiring adjusted barrel temperature profiles to maintain equivalent gelatinisation degrees.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-10760","field":"abstract","quote":"specific mechanical energy decreased by 23% at pilot scale, necessitating adjusted barrel temperature profiles to maintain equivalent gelatinisation degrees"}]}],"fit":"partial","fitReason":"The researcher's starch–protein composite work addresses biodegradable barrier films and processing science relevant to compostable film development [R1044, SYN-PUB-02373, SYN-PUB-02398, SYN-PUB-10760], but does not directly cover seal strength to rPET tooling, anti-fog performance, or EN 13432 certification pathways required by the challenge."}
